status: Native stale-update defect reproduced and minimally fixed; update concurrency formal verification remains pending
evidence_class: Actual RegistrationStore calls and PostgreSQL state, not execution of the HTTP service or a Lean proof

inputs.keys: One newly generated SDK Ed25519 key; same valid key, slug and deployment through update and replacement
inputs.update_statement: Signed for captured client configuration URI and checked with SDK verifier; signed statement bytes are not logged

sequence: Create seed through actual ordinary registration
Read actual StoredRegistration while present, compare its token digest, validate changed metadata and signed update statement
Commit actual replacement on second owner pool; assert old row absent and complete replacement state
Call actual store.update for the captured old client; record success/error independently
Compare complete deployment, claim, registration and selected role/membership snapshots before and after update
source_boundary: Maps the service authentication read/digest preflight and subsequent store call, but does not execute bearer parsing, service authentication, HTTP routing, service audit or postcommit reload.

baseline.otherwise_unchanged: Claim, complete replacement registration (including statement/token digests and timestamps), selected login privileges and memberships.

fix: Reuse existing SQL queries: update/lock deployment before registration. If the registration update affects zero rows, explicitly roll back the transaction and return Ok(()). This prevents publishing the pending deployment write, aligns deployment-to-registration lock order with replacement, and preserves per-client semantics without a new refusal or API.

validation_scope: No SQL text, schema, SQLx metadata, runtime API or authorization change. Focused native module and existing integration tests plus formatting/strict library Clippy; no repeated Lean/extraction, full Docker gates, deployment or paid model calls.
limits: This proves the deterministic store-level stale-preflight schedule and existing tested registration paths, not every concurrent update/removal interleaving.
The model qualified in registration-transactions-receipt.json explicitly excludes update writers; this native fix does not extend that theorem automatically.
Normal SQL/constraint/transport errors still propagate; no blanket no-op success guarantee for namespace changes or earlier failing statements.
No global equality among replica metadata is imposed; existing per-client update semantics are retained.
PostgreSQL isolation/atomicity/locking/constraints and Core internals remain boundaries; postcommit audit/catalog adoption and deployed behavior are not qualified here.
